question: In a certain code language, 'TROUBLE' is written as '93' and 'COMMUTE' is written as '90'. How will 'FRACTION' be written in that language?
solution:
Explanation:

The positional value table is as follows:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/889ff2be8a048327f450a975a401b2f4241e5f28d86896613386ad4014cb4505.png] 

The pattern followed here is:

Code = Sum of positional values of letters.

 
• In TROUBLE → 93 
 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d3dfe3e61be489f46ed8e48bbfb6498acc8421701adb10c004dd9f32d6ec61ba.png] 
 
• Code = Sum of positional values
 
• Code = 20+18+15+21+2+12+5 = **93**.​​​ 
 
 

 

 
• In COMMUTE → 90 ​
 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/288fe499daa5baa930f873a8d9faf29d28b57c9ffc8e4dedaa9e3a23e35b6f48.png] 
 
• Code = Sum of positional values
 
• Code = 3+15+13+13+21+20+5 = **90**.​​​ 
 
 

 

 
• Similarly, In FRACTION → ​

 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b07223bac07dd02f0f08bc8aeac2e67b365c656fa8b0222044d064cc3f913b98.png] 
 
• Code = Sum of positional values
 
• Code = 6+18+1+3+20+9+15+14 = 86.​​​ 
 
 

We get '86'.

Hence, "Option 1" is the correct answer.
